requirement_table.text: ID register at 0x000 reads 0x20960001.
BUILD register at 0x004 reads the USR_ACCESSE2 word.
SCRATCH at 0x008 reads back the written 32-bit value.
SCRATCH resets to 0.
Unmapped addresses read 0.
A write to an unmapped address changes no register.
h_rdata shows the addressed register within 2 clk cycles of h_re.
h_rdata holds its value until the next h_re.
A write takes effect 1 clk cycle after h_we.
SEL resets to 0.
ACTIVE_SEL is 0 (clock A) after reset.
After a SEL write, ACTIVE_SEL equals SEL once SWITCHING returns to 0.
SWITCHING reads 1 from a change of SEL until the muxed clock has switched.
B_DIV reads a value from 1 to 8 equal to the divide applied to the GT reference clock.
GATE_LEN resets to 25000000.
FREQ_CTRL START reads 0 on the clock after it is written.
A START write begins a gate of GATE_LEN clk cycles.
FREQ_STATUS BUSY is 1 during the gate.
FREQ_STATUS DONE is 1 after the gate ends.
FREQ_COUNT equals the rising edges of the muxed clock in the gate (25000000 for clock A with the default gate).
FREQ_COUNT with clock B selected equals 156250000 divided by B_DIV within 1 count per default gate.
A disagreement between the muxed counter and its Gray twin increments MUX_ERRS by 1.
A muxed counter step that is not exactly +1 increments MUX_ERRS by 1.
MUX_ERRS is 0 after 1000 random switches.
SWITCH_COUNT equals the number of real changes of the active clock after 1000 random switches.
A write to SEL with the value already active leaves SWITCH_COUNT unchanged.
A SNAPSHOT write latches the low 32 bits of the muxed counter into MUX_COUNT, which holds until the next SNAPSHOT.
sfp_tx_disable is 1 at all times.
The design uses 0 GT transceiver channels.
The design uses 1 GT reference clock buffer.
Worst negative slack is 0 ns or more on all constrained paths, with clk_mux and clk in separate asynchronous clock groups.
